directive: Build a $0-stack freelance scope-creep & change-order toolkit priced $9 one-time.

candidates.title: ScopeShield — Zero-Subscription Freelance Change-Order & Scope-Creep Generator
candidates.buyer_persona: Fixed-price freelance developers, designers, and boutique agencies
candidates.recurring_pain: Losing 20%-40% of project margin to casual client 'quick tweak' DMs because drafting formal change orders feels confrontational and proposal suites cost $39-$65/user/mo.
candidates.current_workaround: Absorbing unpaid extra hours or manually rewriting Word/Google Doc addendums
candidates.urgency_signal: Immediate unbilled margin loss and launch-blocker delays

evidence.verbatim_quote: One pro habit you need is dealing with change orders and part of that has to do with whether you have an easier or more difficult client to please. For example, a difficult client will ask for 'tweak' but if you're a pro, you don't bite.
On the flip side I've seen many projects go way over budget when a client is actively involved and introduces scope creep that turns into launch blockers.
This is so true, scope creep is real when the client actively gets involved And when that happens it's better to move the contract to hourly rather having it fixed price
